The user just asked for performance optimizations to increase FPS and reduce lag. I've already addressed three major sources: grass rendering, shadow map size, and adaptive pixel ratio. I applied changes to the renderer initialization to cap the pixel ratio at 1.5 and disabled automatic shadow updates, planning to manually update shadows every other frame. I also reduced the sun's shadow map from 4096 to 2048 and tightened the orthographic frustum. Those edits are done.

Now I need to tackle the next biggest performance hit: the trees. In the current code, trees are built as a massive single instanced mesh with all 620 trunks and a huge number of leaf cards (~10k) that are also included in the shadow pass. This is a lot of draw calls and overdraw, especially when many trees are off-screen. The plan I outlined to the user mentions “Sector the trees into 24 instanced groups so the forest behind you isn’t drawn; distant trees get fewer leaf cards.” To implement that, I must replace the existing tree-building block in index.html with a new implementation that creates multiple instanced groups (sectors) and adds logic to cull or reduce detail for far sectors.

First, I need to locate the current tree-building code in index.html. I recall that earlier in the file there is a section where a geometry for the trunk is created, then an InstancedMesh is built for all tree positions, and leaf cards are added separately. The user didn't request any further edits beyond the renderer and shadow map, so the next logical step is to modify the tree code as promised.

Since the user only asked for a summary of changes, I should respond with a clear statement that I'm now moving on to the tree sectoring.
